messages:
sree: Heads up — design question for envelope encryption across AWS/GCP/Azure KMS in Private deployments. We need guidance on DEK/KEK separation, caching/TTL, KMS call rate smoothing, RBAC (who can unwrap), and audit logging. Thinking of DEK-per-tenant vs DEK-per-instance. cc @leah @tomas

leah: +1. Short answer: DEK per-tenant is safer for data isolation; DEK per-instance helps performance but complicates rotation. For multi-tenant customers we usually do per-tenant DEK and cache it on the serving nodes.

tomas: Agree on per-tenant DEK. For caching: keep DEK in node memory with an LRU and TTL (e.g., 1h default), and persist wrapped DEK in customer row in KVS. Unwrap on first use, then reuse until TTL expires or explicit invalidation.

maya: Key point: call KMS only to unwrap/wrap. Use GenerateDataKey (AWS) or equivalent to create DEKs; never store plaintext DEK on disk. Cache in RAM and evict aggressively on low memory.

leah: For KMS call-frequency smoothing: use a small jittered backoff and batch unwrap requests when ramping up. Avoid thundering herd by adding a singleflight coalescer so only one node unwraps a given tenant DEK at a time.

sree: Singleflight coalescer — good. Any thoughts on TTL durations and rotation windows? What about rotation with minimal availability impact?

tomas: TTL tradeoffs: shorter TTL = fewer long-lived plaintext keys but more KMS traffic. We typically use 15–60m for high-sensitivity customers, 1–6h for general. For rotation: rotate KEK monthly (policy) but rewrap DEKs lazily: rewrap on first unwrap after KEK rotation, with background rewrap job for eager rewrap if needed.

maya: Rewrap approach: when KEK rotates, mark wrapped_DEK metadata with kek_version. On unwrap, if kek_version != current, rewrap DEK with new KEK and update wrapped blob atomically. That avoids mass re-encrypt operations.

leah: RBAC: create a KMS role/principal that only has Decrypt (unwrap) for the KEK and Encrypt for rewrap flows. Never give broad kms:* to app nodes. Use separate IAM roles per cluster/region and limit resource ARNs to specific KEKs.

security-bot: Audit: ensure every KMS call logs a request id and principals. Store KMS request ID, tenant id, operation (GenerateDataKey, Decrypt, Encrypt) and node id in our audit stream. Sample retention: keep full audit for 90d for sensitive tenants, 30d default.

tomas: Also propagate KMS request IDs into our request-trace headers so SLO/tracing correlates latency spikes with KMS latency. For incidents we can trace an unwrap failure back to KMS error codes.

leah: Rate limiting: account for cloud KMS limits. AWS KMS default is fairly low for GenerateDataKey throttles — we should design for 10s-100s reqs/sec per region max, but rely on cache/coalescing to keep steady-state near 0.1–1 reqs/sec per tenant node. Add local token buckets to smooth spikes.

sree: Useful. What about fallback when KMS is unavailable? We can't keep plaintext around, but maybe a short grace-mode using a cached DEK with strict telemetry and limited throughput?

maya: Yes: implement a degraded mode: if KMS unavailable, allow cached DEKs to be used until TTL expires, but rate-limit traffic and surface a high-severity alert. No new DEKs can be created. For long outages, fail closed.

leah: Incident response playbook (short): 1) Detect KMS error rate > X% (alerts). 2) Toggle degraded mode -> allow in-memory DEKs only. 3) Notify oncall and increase logging. 4) If KEK suspected compromise, rotate KEK and trigger rewrap / eviction per policy.

sree: Can we include a small config snippet for node-side cache parameters?

ops-bot: ````
# encryptor cache config (example)
cache:
  max_entries: 1024
  ttl_seconds: 3600  # 1h default
  soft_ttl_seconds: 300 # try refresh in background after 5m
  singleflight_window_ms: 50  # coalesce concurrent unwraps
  max_unwrap_per_sec: 5  # token-bucket per-node
  allow_degraded_mode: true
````

leah: Notes on soft_ttl: let cache return DEK while scheduling background refresh to re-unwrap/rewrap; if refresh fails after N tries, evict and fail requests afterward.

maya: Audit design: emit audit event when wrapped_DEK is created/rewrapped and when unwrap occurs. Include: tenant_id, wrapped_key_id (derived id), kek_version, node_id, kms_request_id. Store audit stream in append-only system and send alerts on anomalous patterns (e.g., many unwraps for same tenant).

tomas: Vulnerability triage: if a node is compromised, we assume DEKs in RAM might be exposed. Response: revoke that node's service account, evict its cache via orchestration, rotate KEK and rewrap all DEKs or at minimum rotate DEKs for affected tenants. Have automated playbooks to accelerate this.

sree: Good — can we summarise recommended defaults for RFC?

leah: Sure — draft defaults: DEK scope = per-tenant; cache TTL = 1h; soft refresh = 5m; singleflight coalescing; KEK rotation cadence = 30d (policy) with lazy rewrap + optional eager job; audit retention = 90d high-sensitivity / 30d default; degraded mode allowed but fail-closed for >TTL. RBAC: least privilege KMS roles per cluster.

maya: I'll put this into a short RFC draft and link diagrams + sequence flows. tagging @tomas for unwrap/rewrap implementation details.

sree: Thanks everyone — this is actionable. If anyone has benchmarks for unwrap latency across KMS providers (esp GCP) please paste them here before EOD. :thumbsup:
